The KonMari Method is a rather recent method for the US, but has been quite the rage in Japan. It's a very efficient method of tackling the issue of clutter once and for all. I highly recommend this book.

It's basic premise is taking every single item of a particular genre, piling it up in one area and sorting through it by asking yourself "does this item bring me joy?" and discarding it if it does not. Remember, joy can come in many forms - joy from usefulness, joy from simply finding appreciation in form as opposed to function, etc.

Another gif showing the motion of suspended particles as waves pass through them
Is the yellow circle on the top supposed to be moving in a clockwise circle like that? I'm sorry, I don't know the significance of the yellow circles.

Yep. If you watch the other particles they move in clockwise circles too. At least, the ones close to the surface do. The purpose of the highlighted circles is just to show you what happens to a particle as a wave passes over it. People often think of waves as causing a one dimensional up and down movement, but they actually move things around in a two dimensional cycle.

The point of the gif is to show how objects submerged even half the amplitude of the waves experience a significant reduction in motion. So building your seastead to stay on the surface during a storm means that it has to be much more massive than if you design it to submerge.
